claims.text: HfZrTiTa0.53 has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
The starting alloy exhibits limited strain hardening and poor uniform deformability.
The starting alloy fails rapidly under high-strain-rate adiabatic deformation.
ECAP followed by controlled annealing can produce a bimodal grain structure in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Annealing at approximately 950 °C for 0.5 hours after ECAP will develop the proposed bimodal grain-size distribution.
The proposed bimodal microstructure will contain ultrafine grains of approximately 300 nm and coarse grains of approximately 10 µm.
The approximately 300 nm grains will enhance dislocation accumulation and dynamic strain hardening.
The approximately 10 µm grains will facilitate more uniform plastic flow and provide additional deformability.
Combining ultrafine and coarse grains will distribute strain more evenly.
The bimodal microstructure will delay shear-band initiation, localization, and rapid failure under dynamic loading.
The intervention will increase dynamic yield strength to approximately 900 MPa or higher.
The intervention will increase fracture strain from the 13.5% quasi-static baseline to near 20% under dynamic loading.
Delayed localization will cause a more gradual and controlled release of impact-induced energy.
The predicted improvements apply at strain rates around 10^3 s^-1 under adiabatic dynamic-compression conditions.
The magnitude of improvement will depend on ECAP route, annealing conditions, ultrafine-to-coarse grain proportion, testing temperature, and scale effects.
